I wrote the output and re-checked the cited lines against the pinned tree; I ran no code.

- **Output:** `/home/mara/cwe-bench/sibling2/out/screener/18140.json`
- **Trust decision:** the RootCoord metastore (`internal/metastore/kv/rootcoord/kv_catalog.go`) links each role+object grant to its stored privileges by an ID made from a 64-bit truncated MD5 (`pkg/util/crypto/crypto.go:44-48`). Two grants that get the same ID share one set of privileges and can read, move or delete each other's.
- **`pattern_fit`:** A. All 7 catalog readers and writers of these IDs are changed by the fix, so there are no uncovered routes (Pattern B).
- **Strongest lever:** IDs already saved in etcd. Switching to the full-length hash only stops new collisions. The fix also has to migrate old 16-character IDs, refuse to serve an ID that two grants share, and keep the survivor's privileges when a role or collection is dropped. Some of these sites sit in collection rename/drop code, which a solver could argue is outside RBAC.
- **Biggest red flag:** none of the listed flags apply. The main risk is fairness: the hidden tests expect one specific fail-closed design, down to the error text "shared legacy grantee id", and the tests need etcd. The report must spell out those rules, or the tests need loosening.
